newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK Sept M0 data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK Sept M0 data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to September M0 data which showed a rise of 7.0 percent year/year.
The consensus forecast was for a month/month rise of 0.4 percent and a year/year increase of 6.9 percent.
"The money supply figures are consistent with what we've seen before, showing still-strong monetary growth."

"M0 appears to be slower than expected. A lot of it seems to be down to banker's operational deposits which is something that fluctuates from month to month, so I don't regard it as being a dramatic slowdown. Retail sales were exceptionally strong in August and a lot of people would have expected them to slow in September and the M0 number does give us a little bit of evidence to suggest that may have happened."
JEREMY HAWKINS/ROB HAYWARD, BANK OF AMERICA

"The data are stronger than expected and should further undermine hopes that base rates may be cut one more time. The jump in consumer credit is additional evidence of the pickup in the consumer sector and ought to imply strong retail sales down the road."
